title: 15 Things You Need to Get Right Before Launching a New Hotel, Resort, Villa or Guest House. Did you know ?
text:
Starting a new resort, villa, hotel or guest house is not an easy job. My recommendation is to never open a property without first testing the basics and making sure everything is in place.

Today, we are going to explore the 15 things you need to do when launching your own hotel, resort, villa, apartment or guest house.

My name is Ravneet Bhalla, and welcome to today's masterclass on launching a hotel/property.

Since 2017, we have worked with more than 100 hotels, villas and apartments, helping them with property launches, online distribution, OTA listings, technology and revenue management.

These are the things we generally keep in mind while launching a property. This is my personal perspective on what I believe is an ideal process. There can be other approaches, and I am not here to compete with, judge or comment on them. This is simply what I believe works.

1. Register Your Business

First, decide how you want to operate your business. It could be a proprietorship, partnership, LLP or private limited company.

Get your business registration documents ready. You will need a PAN, GST registration wherever applicable, and the relevant business details.

Register your business in a way that supports the brand you intend to build. Your business identity should have value and should ideally resonate with your hotel or property name.

2. Get Your Financial and Banking Documents Ready

This is very important because you will need these details for OTA onboarding and receiving payments.

Keep your PAN, GST certificate wherever applicable, current bank account details, cancelled cheque and authorised signatory documents ready.

You need a proper bank account where your booking payments can be transferred.

Without the necessary business and banking documents, getting your property listed on online platforms can become difficult.

3. Arrange Your Property Documents

This is one of the most important steps.

You need valid property documents, whether you own the property or have taken it on lease.

If you have leased a property, there should be a valid lease agreement between the property owner and  lessee. 

Let me give you an example. If Jagat Nath ji owns a property and Baluni ji takes that property on lease, the lease agreement should clearly mention the names of both parties and establish the rental arrangement.

The latest electricity bill should also reflect the property owner's name, and the lease agreement should establish Balun ji as the authorised lessee.

These documents are important because OTAs may ask for them during property verification and onboarding. Most importantly you have to confirm that the person from who you are renting out the property to ensure that the person is legal owner of the property and has rights to lease it out to you. Alot many times People who have leased the property may sublease it to you at a higher cost without informing the original owner which can be a legal issue later on. 

We generally recommend keeping all these documents ready before starting the listing process. You may additionally need to show case govt id proof with address of the owner to match the same on electricity bill. 

4. Get Your Local Licences and Approvals

Make a list of all the licences and permissions required to operate your property.

Depending on the city, location and property category, these may include:

Fire NOC

FSSAI registration or licence if you are serving food

Tourism department registration, wherever applicable

Shops and Establishments registration

Local panchayat or municipal permissions

Building occupancy approvals

Any other locally required licences

Tourism registration is particularly important in destinations such as Goa, where applicable property registrations and approvals need to be taken care of.

Do your homework and understand the local requirements before opening your property.

5. Finalise Your Property Name and Positioning

Decide what you want to call your property and, more importantly, how you want to position it in the market. Pick a name that is not with the compset and competitor, that doesnt violate a trade mark or existing legal name. Do not pick brand names that could cause trouble for you. Remember your property name would ideally reflect in domain name of the website. Please do pick something that has an availability in domain space. 

Is it going to be a resort, villa, business hotel, boutique property, luxury resort, serviced apartment or guest house? You also need to decide how you want to categorise and present your property to customers.

If you are planning to use a star category, make sure it is supported by the appropriate recognition or classification. Do not simply position a guest house as a four-star luxury resort because it sounds more attractive.

Your property positioning should reflect what you actually offer.

6. Set Up Your Website, Email and Contact Details

Your business needs a proper online identity. Get your website, professional business email ID and official contact number ready. While starting with Gmail is okay, its good to have a corporate id. 

You can explore Zoho Mail for professional email accounts. Zoho offers a free option in certain configurations, so if you do not want to spend money initially, it is worth exploring.Make sure your website and contact details represent the property professionally.

7. Invest in Professional Photography

This is extremely important, especially from a revenue management and online distribution perspective.

If you do not have a budget for professional property photography, my suggestion would be to reconsider launching the property until you can arrange it.

In the most humblest possible manner, I have to say this that you are wasting the time of your revenue manager, content team and reservations team, sales team if you do not have good photographs to sell the property. You need quality photographs in landscape format, not just portrait images. Potrait images end up looking bad on a OTA. 

Make sure you cover the facade, reception, swimming pool, rooms, bathrooms, common areas, parking and other facilities.

Good photographs help you present the property properly and give potential guests a reason to consider booking. Bad photos you dont really have to do anything. :) 

8. Finalise Your Room Categories and Inventory, Amenities

Decide exactly what you are selling.

How many rooms do you have? What are the room sizes? What amenities and facilities are available? Do you have different views or different room configurations?

Prepare all these details before creating your OTA listings.

Once you have finalised the room specifications, decide on the room category names. My suggestion is to use names that are catchy, attractive and easy to sell.

For example, if you have a beach property, you could use names such as Tropical Chalet or Premium Chalet rather than simply calling it a Cottage. 

If you have rooms next to the garden and pool, then they can be labelled as Deluxe Room Garden Side, Deluxe Rooms Pool Side. Customers are more than happy to pay for an upgrade to room pool side. 

The way you name and present your room categories makes a difference to how you sell them online. 

Setup the right amenities, Liquid Soap/Shampoo/Moisturizer Dispenser will save you more money than buying small soap bars, shampoo bottles etc. If you are into a mid segment and providing items such as slippers, dental kit is not fitting your budget, keep a small stock and mention on request at a charge. You can always waive it off for an Important Client or to build loyalty. Tea Coffee Maker, bottled water is a must. These amenities are basic requirements as seen by travellers. 

9. Prepare Your Hotel Policies

Before accepting bookings, decide on your property policies.

Are you pet-friendly? Are you couple-friendly? What are your check-in and check-out timings?

You should also finalise your payment policies, cancellation policies and other guest-related terms and conditions.

These details should be clear before you start receiving reservations.

10. Arrange Your Hotel Operations and Guest Amenities

Make sure the property is operationally ready before opening.

You need to arrange your linen, towels, toiletries, cleaning supplies, housekeeping equipment, laundry arrangements and maintenance support.

Everything required for the day-to-day running of the property should be in place.

Do not wait for your first guest to arrive before realising that basic operational arrangements are missing.

11. Set Up Your Hotel Technology

Technology is an important part of running a hospitality business today.

You should look at setting up:

Property Management System

Channel Manager

Booking Engine

Let me give you an example. Foodle Plus offers a PMS, Point of Sale and Guest Experience Management System, which we call GEMS.

You can also explore channel managers such as STAAH, which can integrate and synchronise with your PMS.

Having the right technology in place makes it easier to manage reservations, room availability and day-to-day operations.

12. Get Your Property Listed on OTAs

Once your documents, photographs, room categories and other property details are ready, you can start the OTA onboarding process.

This is where all the work you have done in the previous steps comes together.

Your property content, room details, photographs, policies and business documents will be required during the listing process.

Make sure the information you provide is accurate and consistent across platforms.Do not simply focus on getting listed on every OTA without understanding how much business you are actually generating. List with the right photos, amenities, policies and pricing that help you attract customers.

Getting listed is important, but remember that listing a property and generating business from it are two different things.

13. Work Out Your Pricing and Revenue Strategy

This is where things become really important. 

Focus on 

Parent Website 

OTA's (Online Travel Agencies:

Promote direct business via GMB and other sources- Just dial. 

Reach out to b2b partners and agents 

Create sales offices and consolidators, GSA

Whether you are focusing towards occupancy or ADR or a balance choice of revpar. The answer has to be balanced basis of market, judgement, hotel strength and USP, challenges. This cannot be based on "because i said so". 

Most OTAs work on a commissionable business model. So, getting listed online is one thing, but consistently generating business at the right price is another. Do not get scared of commissions. Alot of Revenue management firms/managers will talk about OTA commissions and that they will hurt you in long term. Remember your price is in your hand and play dynamic with rates to make up for the commission structure. OTA's will get you guests from across the globe who will eventually become your patrons and convert directly. Your visibility is under your control. 

Your pricing, distribution and revenue strategy need to work together. Draft out your offline pricing, B2B agents and protect them, at the same time sell at B2C and build loyalty. The objective should be to generate the right business for your property rather than simply increasing the number of bookings. Build a funnel for offline and direct business as well. 

14. Set Up Guest Safety and Compliance

Guest safety is something you should never compromise on.

Make sure you have the necessary fire safety arrangements, emergency exits, first aid facilities and other safety requirements in place.

Your guests should feel comfortable and secure when they stay at your property.

Pay attention to the basic safety and compliance requirements before opening.

15. Do a Soft Launch and Test Everything

Lastly, never open your property without testing it first.

Invite your friends and family to stay at the property. Let them experience the rooms and test everything.Ask them to check the minibar, sofa, beds, room condition, air conditioning and other facilities.

Let them experience the property as actual guests would.You will identify problems that you may not have noticed while setting up the hotel.Get those problems resolved before you start welcoming paying guests.

Final Thoughts

Opening a hospitality business is not easy. It is not just about preparing rooms and getting your property listed online in the right manner.

You need to get your paperwork right, complete the necessary approvals, prepare your operations, invest in the right technology and, most importantly, have a revenue strategy.

Since 2013, I have seen properties with excellent locations struggle because their pricing was wrong, their operations were not organised, they did not have the right technology or they did not have the right people in place.

At Towno, we work with hospitality businesses across multiple destinations and property categories, helping them grow through online distribution, technology implementation and revenue management.

If you are planning to launch a property and are unsure where to start, feel free to connect with me.

Reach out to Towno, and my team and I will be happy to help you set up your hotel and get it ready for business.

title: The Biggest Mistake Hotels Make When Handling Difficult Guests, How to do Better ?
text:
Having spent more than a decade in Hospitality, Earlier with makemytrip and then as a budding Entrepreneur on supply side with Hotels, Resorts, Airbnbs and much more. 
We have dealt with complaints, escalations, and tough guests every single day left right and centre. 

But then I came across The Empty Boat Theory. 

The Empty Boat Theory.
I am sure you would have read about this, on Linkedin Posts, Instagram and so on but did you understand this ? 

The Theory goes like this, 
Lets say you are in a boat, Moving/Still across a river or stream and an another boat crashes into your boat. I would be angry. 
Furious is the right term possibly, with loads of curses thrown towards the other person in the boat about how incompetent they are, they did it purposefully, Immature, Childish, not a responsible person and so on. 

But what if the boat is empty. An empty Ghost Boat that came from somewhere and hit your boat. Then there is no one to blame, none to curse, no tantrum to throw. 
The person then adjusts and moves on, accepting what has happened, has happened. 

THIS IS What Happens In A Hotel. 

An angry guest shouting at the front desk team. 
A Lady creating a scene, 
A Gentleman cursing at a Waiter, 
A Negative review feels unfair.
An agent sounds rude.

An assumption flashes through our minds, 
“They are disrespecting us.”
“They don’t value our service.”
" These guests are like this only " 
" North Indians are like this only " 

A recent clip went viral where a hotel staff in goa said, we do not want guests from North India, they are rude or difficult. How did we reach here ? What was the thought process ? Something must have happened for a person to feel this. 

But what if in all its possibility, it’s just an empty boat?
Maybe:
• The guest had a terrible journey. 
• Their previous hotel ruined their trip
• They’re dealing with something personal. 
• The girl had a breakup. 
• The boy lost his father. 
• The Couple Lost their Pet. 

Anything can happen. 

This is where We understand the issue, 

* Not every reaction deserves a reaction
* Not every complaint is personal
* And not every situation needs escalation

Understand the issue and work towards resolution without taking things personally. As soon as this happens, Service team starts delivering better service.
Because real hospitality is not just service.
It’s emotional intelligence at scale.
And that’s the difference between a good hotel and a great one.

At Foodle+ , We believe great service starts with clarity, not chaos.
No missed requests.
No broken communication.
No frustration building up.
When systems are working, there is action and not a reaction. 

Lets act on the issue instead of Reacting to the issue. 
Have you ever had such an issue ? 
Comment and Share Your Experience :)

title: Hotel/Resort Operations- The Underrated Driver of Hospitality Revenue
text:
Sales Brings Revenue, Operations decide whether it will stay or not. 
Operations- The Underrated Driver of Revenue

2026, When revenue managers are chasing Revpar and Occupancy, but none is bothered about actually solving the problem.
There is a silent killer in hotels, and while everyone is running behind Occupancy, ARR, Revpar etc. People have forgotten what forms the backbone of the industry. 

Operations- the backbone of hotel industry, the vajra of hospitality. Often ignored at multiple levels, this is a dangerous gap. 
Revenue is not just filling up rooms, Its also about what you deliver vs what a customer experiences.
A guest waiting for an early checkin, Rooms are available but yet they have to wait. Worst, a customer waiting after check in time because check outs werent initiated at time. Customers dialing for towels in room, basic toiletries, Ac not working, Tv remote not working. 

All of this sounds familiar right ? But this doesnt reach the GM or the owner. 
There is lack of coordination within the department, who ends up suffering ? Guess ? 
Yes, we have 80% occupancy for today, but in reality the experience is a nightmare for someone who trusted you while booking the same.
A guest wont remember whether you ran a LMD or EBO or what your pricing strategy was. 
What do they recall ? 
A Dirty Room, Non Functional AC, TV that doesnt Turn On, Geyser that looks new but no hot water in the tap, A Complain that couldnt go through, A Phone that kept on ringing, A Nightmare. 

These arent issues, these are broken promises. I remember when i was pitching my idea about stronger operations to a 4 star luxury hotel, the manager asked me. 
" Ravneet, what are we trying to achieve, Why are we trying to Solve Something That is NOT Broken ?"

This is when i realised, on paper everything is good, 80-90% occupancy, hitting the revenue but not addressing the issue. 
Issue being " Lack Of Ownership", 
Instead of Automating the operations, Trying to provide the best experience to the customer, we are more focused on painting the rooms, buying the latest TV, placing the Italian Rug. 
None is actively or proactively checking if the "Guest Is Comfortable".

Bad reviews are not the biggest critic or damage to the hotel. Its the Silent Churn, Guests who came, Stayed, Did not argue, Did not leave a feedback. 
No Repeat bookings, No Referrals, No Second chance, 
This is revenue loss that you cannot see in a report. 

With Foodle+ our team is trying to empower the staff to solve problems instead of just escalating issues. To enable more for your customer in experience and in return get higher conversions, reviews forming strong operations. 
Happy Guests will review, post, refer, spend more and most importantly understand if you fail sometime. 

This is Real ARR, not compounded, not just booked but earned.
